title: Read My Bible — Intent (product brief)
summary: Approved 2026-09-03 product brief for the October 2026 Read My Bible campaign (Favor Church, owner Rico Tiongson, repo favorchurch/readmybible-app.favor.church). Why: Favor reads Matthew one chapter a day through October inside Connect Groups; check-ins earn coins that pool into a group home that grows tent -> mansion; encouragement within a group, never competition between people. Audiences: Connect Group member (Rock Auth0 login, own group, check in); leader/assistant leader (same plus join code, QR, and a quiet 'hasn't read today' list); section leaders on Rock Group Type 24 (department, cluster, region, campus) with an admin dashboard and progress timeline; person with no group (solo progress, campus group leaderboard, join by code). Success criteria: real person logs in at readmybible-app.favor.church via Auth0 and lands on their real Rock roster; check-ins persist and update coins/home for the group; join-by-code writes membership to Rock and the app reflects it; admin dashboard shows section hierarchy with per-group ratios and a timeline chart; phone and tablet layouts; live/tested by 2026-09-06, leaders onboard 2026-09-20, campaign starts 2026-10-01. Non-goals at launch: push/email reminders, multiple reading plans, social sharing, Tagalog scripture, Rock photo avatars, individual rankings. Constraints: Rock production is source of truth for people/groups/roles/campus; only two kinds of Rock writes (the rico+test fixture memberships and the join-by-code GroupMember insert); everything else in Supabase project shared-apps-favor-church schema readmybible; Redis on redis.favor.church with every key prefixed readmybible:<env>:; never mention Fluro; copy follows the speak-like-favor brand voice.

title: Read My Bible — Game Rules (plan, scoring, stages)
summary: Canonical game rules, faithful to the original prototype in app/page.tsx. Reading plan: Matthew, 28 chapters; day n = October n 2026 = Matthew chapter n for n in 1..28; October 29-31 are grace days (no new chapter, catch-up allowed); the window closes at end of October 31 in the reader's timezone. Check-in: honor-based ('I read today'); one check-in per person per chapter, re-tap is a no-op; catch-up allowed for any past day in the window, never a future day; 'today' is the device local date, client sends readingDate (YYYY-MM-DD) plus its IANA timezone, server accepts 2026-10-01 through the client's local today with one day of clock-skew tolerance; a check-in stores the group the person was in at that moment (group_id) or null for solo. Personal scoring: 10 coins per chapter; streak = consecutive reading dates ending today or yesterday in the reader's timezone; medals at 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 chapters; a next-trophy bar toward the next medal threshold; coins never decrease and leaving a group keeps personal coins. Group scoring: with M = active Rock members (roles Member 23, Leader 24, Assistant Leader 81) and C = check-ins carrying that group_id, ratio = C / (M * 28) clamped to [0,1] so a group of 5 and a group of 15 grow at the same pace. Home stage thresholds by ratio: Tent 0, Trailer 0.10, Cabin 0.25, Apartment 0.45, House 0.65, Mansion 0.85. Connect tab shows group coin total (C * 10), stage, and a bar to the next stage; 'N of M have read today' counts distinct members with a check-in dated today in their own timezone. Campus leaderboard: scope is the group's Rock campus (Group.CampusId), or Person.PrimaryCampusId when solo; groups ranked by ratio, tie-break readers today then name; individuals are never ranked anywhere ('We cheer for groups, not against people'). Copy anchors kept from the prototype: 'Make space for the Word today.', 'Read anywhere. Grow together.', 'This is an honor-based check-in. Take your time.', 'Grace for the missed days. Joy in the next one.'

title: Read My Bible — User Flows (mermaid diagrams)
summary: Four mermaid flow/sequence diagrams for the app's core journeys. (1) Login and landing: open app -> session check -> Auth0 login (email OTP / Google / Facebook) -> Rock post-login Action sets the rock_person_id claim -> if rock_person_found is false show the not-found screen pointing to the Connect Group leader, else the server loads active Group Type 25 memberships cached 5 minutes; one membership goes straight to the Today tab, several show a group picker defaulting to the leader group, none drops into solo mode with join-by-code. (2) Daily check-in sequence: reader calls checkIn(chapter, readingDate, tz); the server action validates the date window, timezone, and membership, inserts a checkin row unique on person+chapter, DELs the Redis keys group:{id}:stats and campus:{id}:board, and returns coins, streak, medals, and group stage. (3) Join a group by code: leader opens the Connect tab and gets a 4-character code (e.g. F52A) plus a QR to /join/{code}; the member hits /join/{code} login-gated; the app GETs Rock GroupMembers by PersonId and GroupId, POSTs a new GroupMembers row with role 23 Active if absent, or PATCHes an inactive row back to Active, busts the person cache, and lands them on the Today tab in the new group. Codes are four characters from the ambiguity-free alphabet ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789, one per group, minted the first time a leader opens the tab; joining requires being logged in with a resolved Rock person. (4) Admin dashboard: /admin gates on allowlist or active Group Type 24 membership (403 with a link home otherwise); scope resolves to the global root for allowlist users or the member's own sections for GT24; Rock supplies the section subtree, GT25 groups, and member counts cached 15 minutes; renders a hierarchy tree with campus, members, readers today, ratio, and stage per group, a timeline chart of daily ratio from Oct 1 to today, and a CSV export.

title: Read My Bible — Technical Spec (stack, auth, Rock access, data model, routes)
summary: The original build spec. Stack: Next.js App Router + TypeScript on Vercel (team Favor Church, domain readmybible-app.favor.church), pnpm, @auth0/nextjs-auth0 v4 on tenant favorchurch.au.auth0.com client "Rock Web Apps", Supabase project shared-apps-favor-church (ref ixyntblebucvslqexcqh) Postgres schema readmybible with Drizzle + postgres-js and drizzle-kit migrations, node-redis v5 keyed readmybible:{prod|preview:<branch>|local}:, Chart.js via react-chartjs-2 for admin only, hand-built components on app/globals.css with Tailwind v4 available, Vitest for game rules and scripture parsing plus a pnpm build gate. Removed during setup: vinext, wrangler, @cloudflare/vite-plugin, vite.config.ts, .openai/, .wrangler/, worker/, examples/, app/chatgpt-auth.ts, tests/rendered-html.test.mjs, the SQLite Drizzle config; next.config.ts stopped ignoring TS and lint errors. Auth: Auth0 middleware mounts /auth/login, /auth/callback, /auth/logout; issuer is the custom domain https://auth.favor.church; the Rock post-login Action reads the callback hostname and readmybible-app.favor.church is registered in SOURCE_CONFIG_BY_HOST mapping to production Rock (three Actions redeployed with pnpm run deploy); claims used are https://auth.favor.church/rock_person_id and rock_person_found, and a missing claim renders the not-found screen; locally Auth0 maps localhost to rock-preview so DEV_MOCK_PERSON_ID (honored only when NODE_ENV !== production, never set on Vercel) substitutes a Rock prod PersonId; Vercel preview URLs are unmapped in Auth0 and cannot log in, so previews are build verification only. Rock access: all calls go through lib/rock/client.ts, REST v1, header Authorization-Token: ROCK_API_KEY against ROCK_API_URL=https://rock.favor.church/api, using a RestUser named readmybible-app.favor.church (initially Rock Administrator, with a rock-security follow-up to narrow it). Cached reads: Person People/{id} (Id, NickName, FirstName, LastName, PrimaryCampusId) 5 min; memberships GroupMembers filtered PersonId + Active + GroupRoleId 23/24/81 with $expand=Group then client-filtered to GroupTypeId 25, IsActive, not archived, 5 min; section memberships same query kept to GroupTypeId 24, 5 min; roster GroupMembers by GroupId Active with $expand=Person, 5 min; campus groups Groups filtered GroupTypeId 25, CampusId, IsActive, not archived plus member counts, 15 min; section subtree Groups by ParentGroupId recursively until GroupTypeId 25, 15 min. Writes: join by code POSTs GroupMembers {GroupId, PersonId, GroupRoleId 23, GroupMemberStatus 1} or PATCHes an existing inactive row to Active, then busts the person's cache keys and logs to join_events; the fixture is rico+test (PersonId 13358) in group 24077 cycled Member -> Leader 24 -> removed. Role IDs 23, 24, 81, 22, 68 are production values living in lib/rock/constants.ts with a note that preview differs. Data model in schema readmybible: profiles (rock_person_id PK, display_name, avatar jsonb, translation default NET, active_group_id, timestamps); checkins (id bigserial, rock_person_id, group_id nullable, chapter smallint 1..28, reading_date, timezone, created_at, unique(rock_person_id, chapter)); join_codes (group_id PK, code char(4) unique, created_by, created_at); join_events (id, group_id, rock_person_id, code, outcome, created_at). Indexes on checkins(group_id, reading_date) and checkins(rock_person_id); Supabase anon and service roles get no grants, the app connects as a dedicated readmybible_app Postgres role with search_path readmybible. Routes and actions: / (four-tab app, server component loads session context), /join/[code] (login-gated), /admin, /admin/export.csv, /not-found-in-rock, actions checkIn(chapter, readingDate, tz), saveProfile(profile), chooseGroup(groupId), and GET /api/scripture?ref=&t= backed by a provider adapter with 30-day Redis cache. Scripture popups: one curated key passage per Matthew chapter in lib/plan.ts (28 entries) opening a popup with the reader's translation and an "Open in Bible.com" link https://www.bible.com/bible/{id}/MAT.{chapter}.{code} with ids NET 107, ESV 59, CSB 1713, NIV 111, NLT 116; providers in lib/scripture/ were originally NET via labs.bible.org (no key), ESV via api.esv.org (ESV_API_KEY), NLT via api.nlt.to (NLT_API_KEY), CSB and NIV via API.Bible (API_BIBLE_KEY, NIV pending approval), with a missing key or provider error degrading to reference plus Bible.com link only. Admin: ADMIN_PERSON_IDS (starting with 152) sees the global Connect root, otherwise any active Group Type 24 membership sees that subtree, everyone else 403; content is a collapsible section hierarchy with campus/members/readers today/ratio/stage per group, a daily cumulative ratio line chart from Oct 1, and a CSV export. Env vars: AUTH0_DOMAIN=auth.favor.church, AUTH0_CLIENT_ID=aX24IzeDb69BQ1KNtTqnilbmvdRxV3TO, AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET, AUTH0_SECRET, APP_BASE_URL, ROCK_API_URL, ROCK_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, REDIS_KEY_PREFIX=readmybible:prod:, ADMIN_PERSON_IDS=152, optional ESV_API_KEY / NLT_API_KEY / API_BIBLE_KEY, and local-only DEV_MOCK_PERSON_ID. Responsive: phone first 360-430px, tablet 768-1024px gets two columns for Connect and Progress. Observability: Vercel logs and analytics only, with structured one-line JSON logs on Rock writes and provider failures.

title: Read My Bible — Design System (tokens, frames, type scale, motion, states)
summary: Machine-readable design system for the M2 lanes (Today, Connect, Progress and Rewards, Admin and onboarding) and for anyone editing app/globals.css, app/styles/*.css, or app/admin/admin.css. Palette rule (issue 32 decision D2): the eight named color tokens keep their hues for the life of the product -- --navy, --coral, --gold, --sage, --cream, --paper, --blue, --violet. A screen may add a new tone of one of those hues (soft tint, deeper shade, a neutral derived from navy or cream) but never a new hue family, never dark mode, never a replacement for a primary token; fonts (--font-sans, --font-display) and the in-app icon set (components/nav-icon.tsx, public/avatar-*) are frozen outright. Existing color tokens: --navy #172943 (primary text, primary button, brand ink), --coral #d96c57 (reading card, active nav state, emphasis), --gold #e7a72f (reward and focus ring), --sage #91a88b (success, completed read), --cream #f7f0df (app shell background), --paper #fffaf0 (card and sheet surface), --blue #7b9caf and --violet #9c84ab (avatar tints). New D2-compliant tones: --ink = var(--navy), --ink-2 #687485 (secondary text), --ink-muted #6e716d (tertiary text, timestamps, helper copy), --surface-1 = var(--cream), --surface-2 = var(--paper), --surface-3 #eae4d6 (deeper emphasis neutral), --line rgba(23,41,67,.14), --line-strong rgba(23,41,67,.28), --coral-soft #f4d6d0, --coral-deep #9c4e3f, --gold-soft #f9e9cb, --sage-soft #e0e7df, --navy-soft #e3e5e8. Spacing: 4px base, nine steps --space-1..--space-9 = 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64px; existing hand-tuned values need not migrate. Radius: --radius-sm 4, --radius-md 8, --radius-lg 14, --radius-xl 20, --radius-pill 999px. Motion tokens: --dur-fast 120ms (press feedback), --dur-base 200ms (page transitions, nav state), --dur-slow 320ms (celebratory motion); --ease-out cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1) for anything entering or responding to input, --ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.65, 0, .35, 1) for motion that starts and ends at rest. Shadows: --shadow-sm for resting cards, --shadow-md for elevated surfaces such as open sheets. Frame vocabulary (app/styles/frame.css) sets a screen's outer width without replacing internal spacing: .frame 1040px is the default full product screen (Today, Connect, Rewards, Progress, Admin); .frame--focused 560px for a single decision or short flow (group picker, solo join, onboarding); .frame--rail is .frame width with a main column plus optional secondary rail whose children are .frame__main and .frame__rail; .frame__span crosses both grid tracks. .frame--rail collapses to one column below 1024px and also above 1024px when .frame__rail is absent or empty via :has(> .frame__rail) -- this is the fix for the bug the run existed to close, an ordinary Connect member must never see a reserved empty second column where Leader Tools would be. Breakpoints are additive at 480, 768, 1024px on top of the existing 360-389px range (the max-width: 370px rules keep behaving). Type scale: Display clamp(38px, 9vw, 64px) for hero headings; H1 24-27px; H2 18-24px; H3 15-16px; Body 16px; Small 13px; Micro 11px decorative only (all-caps eyebrows and single-letter abbreviations, never the only source of meaning -- anything a reader must read sits at 12px or above). Intentional Georgia exceptions: every other Georgia declaration is a leftover the sans system in typography.css overrides by selector, and tests/css-rules.test.ts fails the build on a new unlisted one; the two sanctioned serif selectors are .quick-verse-button strong (app/styles/today.css, the chapter and verse reference such as "Matthew 8:23-27") and .passage-text (app/styles/sheet.css, the Scripture passage body in the Quick Verse popup), both marked with a /* serif-exception */ comment. The same test enforces no font-size at 11px or below unless the line carries /* decorative */. Interaction states, carried by every baseline control (.primary-button, .secondary-link, .close-button, .bottom-nav button, .picker-option, .header-person, the calendar buttons): default resting style; hover only inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) so touch never sticks; focus-visible as a 3px var(--gold) outline at 3px offset (plain buttons inherit the global button:focus-visible rule, non-button controls declare it); active translateY(1px) or scale(.98) whichever suits the shape; disabled opacity .55 with cursor not-allowed and no hover lift, no extra markup. Controls triggering a pending action carry aria-busy alongside disabled. Motion rules: a single global rule in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) in app/styles/motion.css targets *, *:before, *:after so a new keyframe never needs its own opt-out; no animation loops (.spark's infinite twinkle now plays once and holds); pageIn uses --dur-base and --ease-out; new animation animates transform and opacity only, never width, height, or layout properties; no autoplay confetti, no scroll-jacking, no self-repeating decorative animation. Lanes must not reinvent page frames, tokens, the Sheet component, or the display helpers in lib/plan.ts and lib/game.ts -- extend them rather than forking; lane-local custom properties belong in that lane's stylesheet, never in :root.

title: Read My Bible — Decisions log (Q1-Q25, D2, D5, D-favicon, D-location, D-csb-niv-source, D-popup-serif)
summary: The decision log for Read My Bible, the authoritative source for the decision IDs still cited in code comments across the repo. Three blocks. BLOCK 1 -- grilling, 2026-09-03, IDs Q1-Q25 plus Misc: Q1 domain readmybible-app.favor.church on Vercel, retiring OpenAI Sites and vinext. Q2 Supabase project shared-apps-favor-church, schema readmybible, Drizzle; Neon rejected for lack of CLI access. Q3 Matthew 1-28 mapped to Oct 1-28 with grace days after; verse popups in-app plus a Bible.com link. Q4 show the person's own Group Type 25 group, a picker when there are several, solo mode plus join-by-code or QR when there are none; GT24 leaders get the admin view; connect.favor.church linked where natural. Q5 group progress is the ratio of chapters read to members x 28. Q6 any past day in the window may be backdated, never a future day; streaks are computed by reading date. Q7 the full Rock roster is shown, first name only. Q8 leaders see the join code and a "hasn't read today" list. Q9 fixture person rico+test in group 24077 exercised as Member, then Leader, then removed. Q10 the wayfinder map and tickets live as GitHub issues on this repo. Q11 scope is every active GT25 group, all age groups. Q12 the device timezone decides "today" (multi-campus). Q13 use the latest packages that build on Vercel, with Auth0 SDK v4. Q14 in scope: an admin dashboard with Chart.js; out of scope: reminders, multiple plans, a campus progress tab. Q15 test by Sunday 2026-09-06, leaders from 2026-09-20, product name "Read My Bible". Q16 join-by-code writes the GroupMember row to Rock production using a new REST key, Rock Administrator for now with a narrowing issue filed in rock-security. Q17 campus-scoped group leaderboard; individuals are never ranked; the prototype scoring is kept. Q18 campus scope comes from the group, or PrimaryCampusId when solo. Q19 translation toggle over NET, ESV, CSB, NIV, NLT, defaulting to NET, English only. Q20 admin access is an allowlist plus any GT24 membership scoped to its subtree. Q21 admin shows hierarchy titles plus per-group stats and a timeline ratio chart from Oct 1. Q22 social share retired. Q23 Auth0 host mapping, Action redeploy, and callback URLs approved; preview URLs stay unmapped; local dev uses a mock session. Q24 everything ships by Sunday. Q25 (2026-09-03) narrows Q4's "connect.favor.church linked where natural": that portal is internal to Connect Group leaders only, never members or the public, so it was removed from the not-found screen, the auth-error screen, and solo mode, and kept only inside the leader-gated Connect tools box. Misc: missing assets may be generated with codex imagegen (luna), and Rico adds the REST key to .env himself. BLOCK 2 -- Issue 32 UI/UX audit, 2026-09-03, plan docs/plans/issue-32-ui-ux-implementation.md, IDs D2, D5, D-favicon, D-location: D2 the palette may evolve in tones, accents, and neutrals only -- the eight named color tokens (--navy, --coral, --gold, --sage, --cream, --paper, --blue, --violet) keep their hues for the life of the product, new tones of those hues are allowed (for example --coral-soft, --ink-muted), but never a new hue family, never dark mode, and never a replacement for a primary token; --ink-muted was darkened from #6e716d to #646765 during the run to clear the 4.5:1 body-text contrast floor. D5 introduces the dev-only clock override DEV_MOCK_TODAY (a YYYY-MM-DD date) honored only when NODE_ENV !== "production", the same guard DEV_MOCK_PERSON_ID already used, with lib/dev-clock.ts as the only reader, production behavior unchanged, and a two-sided test proving the guard; it exists so the active, grace, and closed states could be QA'd before the real October 1 launch. D-favicon replaced the leftover Next.js starter grid asset with an open book and a small tent silhouette, --navy on --cream with a coral accent, regenerated at 16px and 32px, with no other icon or font asset changed. D-location removed the reading-location picker (the catch-up flow's "Where did you read?" question and its LOCATIONS state) because it captured a location that was never sent anywhere and added a step to an honor-based check-in for no product purpose. BLOCK 3 -- Issue 35 Scripture and debug, 2026-09-04, plan docs/plans/issue-35-scripture-and-debug.md, IDs D-csb-niv-source and D-popup-serif: D-csb-niv-source records that bolls.life (the source for NET, KRV, and the other six key-passage versions) does not carry CSB at all and carries only NIV 1984 rather than the 2011 edition Rico specified, so CSB and NIV(2011) key passages (issue #49) were instead sourced from bible.com and biblegateway.com -- two independent licensed republishers of the same copyrighted text -- fetched and cross-checked verse by verse per scripts/build-csb-niv.ts, accepting a passage only when every verse in its range agrees between both sources after normalizing each site's typesetting noise (nbsp padding around quotes and dashes, footnote markers) and never by picking a winner on disagreement; all 28 passages agreed for both versions on the run that produced the committed lib/scripture/data/{CSB,NIV}/key-passages.json, with source URLs and agreed/omitted status recorded in the sibling provenance.json in each version's directory. D-popup-serif records that the Quick Verse passage body renders in Georgia serif at weight 400 in var(--ink), decided by Rico on 2026-09-04 after reviewing amendment 6, for readability and visual separation of Scripture from app chrome, making it the second sanctioned Georgia exception alongside the verse reference.
